body: Manchester United coach Michael Carrick speaks to Sky Sports. “We’re obviously delighted [Amad Diallo is back] … he’s a big part of the group … he offers us an awful lot … it’s nice to have him back … he was looking really good pre-season … he’s close to being back to his best … [Leny Yoro] is at the stage of his career to make the next step … he’s made his debut for France … fully deserved … we look forward to seeing him play … we want to keep moving forward … keep improving … we’ve added a little bit … we’ve had to clean up and sharpen up a few other things … get the balance right … today’s a good time to start.”

The results of the 3pms are in. In the main, it’s been a good afternoon for bottom-placed Spurs: Fulham, Bournemouth and Sunderland all lost, while Aston Villa failed to win, so should Roberto De Zerbi’s men claim all three points this evening, they could catapult up the table as high (realistically) as 14th. Ipswich’s late comeback at Fulham however means Manchester United can only climb as high as 10th with victory here. Sarah Rendell has all the details in today’s Clockwatch.

articles.title: Henderson and João Pedro lead Chelsea charge against Bournemouth
articles.summary: Watch and learn, kids. The day began with one for the youth audience, Cole Palmer appearing on a live stream to explain the thinking behind his latest contract extension, and it ended with the oldest player to join Chelsea during the BlueCo era stealing the show with an all-action midfield display…
body: The Age of Henderson is under way. There was a time when the idea of a 36-year-old starting in midfield for the Chelsea constructed by Clearlake Capital was impossible to imagine, but not any more. The vibe changed when Xabi Alonso joined as manager last summer, leading to a shift in transfer strategy, and the benefit of placing more faith in experience was on show as Jordan Henderson marked his home debut by decorating an excellent performance with two spectacular goals and an assist for Morgan Rogers.

The sense is that Chelsea, who are up to fifth, are better off with Henderson’s leadership. The former Liverpool captain was a surprise signing from Brentford but is determined to make his presence felt. The veteran set the tone against Bournemouth, offering aggression in midfield, and was key to the side’s first league win in four games. Henderson opened the scoring in the second minute and later bent in a free-kick to leave Palmer in the shade.

articles.title: 'What this team has been crying out for' - Renshaw 190 lifts Australia
articles.summary: After nine years and 280 days, Matt Renshaw scores epic century to put Australia on top against South Africa and push his own case for a regular place.
body: Matt Renshaw scored an epic first Test century in more than nine years to put Australia in control of the first Test in their highly anticipated series against South Africa.

After much talk about the issues among their ageing top order on day one, Renshaw ground out a majestic career-best 190 from 397 balls in Durban, emphatically pushing his case to be part of Australia's future.

The 30-year-old was born in Middlesbrough and was a childhood friend of England captain Joe Root - their fathers played together in English club cricket - before his parents left the UK for New Zealand and then Australia when he was seven.
As well as potentially match-defining innings, having dragged Australia from 124-6 to 390 all out, it was a statement knock from Renshaw who has had an in-out international career.

articles.title: Aston Villa’s wait for home win goes on after Ajer hits back for Brentford
articles.summary: Kristoffer Ajer spent a chunk of the extended international window fielding questions about the state of mind of his Norway teammate Erling Haaland and perhaps in recent weeks he also picked up some finishing tips.
body: For the second time in the game, one team cancelled out the other within two minutes, just 88 seconds between Yehor Yarmolyuk’s opener, born from Jaidon Anthony pressing Tyrone Mings, and Nicolas Jackson’s simple equaliser. It was a strange, seesawing and tempestuous game and a busy one for Ajer, who was also booked late on for questioning a decision by the referee, Craig Pawson, who managed the impressive feat of drawing ire from both sets of supporters.

Unai Emery had dipped into expletive to make it clear he was not overly enamoured with Villa’s previous home performance, describing their display in defeat to Nottingham Forest as “very shit”, and his side’s failure to hold on to the lead against Brentford extended their winless record since the Villa Park revamp left the ground with just three stands in play.

This feisty draw also maintained Keith Andrews’s fine, unbeaten record against Emery across four meetings, though the visitors also had chances to snatch victory with the left-back El Hadji Malick Diouf’s delivery into the box keeping Villa’s defenders on their toes and the Brazil striker Igor Thiago a constant threat.

articles.title: Ipswich’s O’Shea and and Outtara stun Fulham with last-gasp comeback win
articles.summary: Ipswich produced a dramatic turnaround to beat Fulham 2-1 after late goals by Abdoul Ouattara and Dara O’Shea extended Álvaro Arbeloa’s winless start to six Premier League matches.
body: The former Real Madrid manager had been on course to toast a maiden league victory in charge of the Cottagers after Ryan Sessegnon’s sweet 55th-minute strike put the visitors ahead. It would have eased the pressure on Arbeloa, but the Spaniard watched his team collapse, with Ouattara producing a spectacular 30-yard equaliser with two minutes left before O’Shea, the Ipswich captain, headed home in stoppage time to spark wild celebrations at Portman Road.

Fulham will spend another week in the relegation zone with only two points from six league games and they are now seven points behind Ipswich. A third win of the campaign for Gary O’Neil’s men has them up to ninth in the table.
Fulham started on the back foot but survived two early corners before the bright Ipswich attacker Julio Enciso curled wide from outside the area.

The visitors’ lackadaisical approach on the ball kept causing self-inflicted problems and their captain, Calvin Bassey, called for calm midway through, which was followed by Arbeloa’s young team slowly starting to gain a foothold.

articles.title: Verstappen beats Ferraris to Singapore pole
articles.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen beats the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton to pole position in qualifying at the Singapore Grand Prix.
body: Verstappen's first lap in final qualifying was enough to take pole, his time fending off a second lap from Leclerc that was 0.054 seconds off pole.
Hamilton was closest to Verstappen after the first runs but was unable to improve on his second run.
In fact, most of the front runners struggled to improve on their second runs, as Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli took fourth on the grid, from McLaren's Lando Norris.
Antonelli's team-mate George Russell was sixth fastest but will drop to the back of the grid with a penalty for using too many engine parts.

articles.title: Rayo Vallecano game abandoned after paper plane protest
articles.summary: Rayo Vallecano's match against Athletic Club was abandoned after the home fans threw paper airplanes onto the pitch in protest against the club's owner.
body: The La Liga game was Rayo's first of the season at the Estadio de Vallecas, which had been temporarily closed after an audit highlighted serious health and safety issues - including a risk of contracting Legionnaires' disease.
Rayo fans blame owner and president Raul Martin Presa, who has long been criticised for the poor upkeep of facilities and a failure to modernise the club.
In the 13th minute of the game, when Rayo fans usually chant "Presa leave now", supporters threw paper planes and small rubber balls on to the pitch.
The referee stopped play and the stadium announcer urged fans not to throw objects on to the pitch, while stewards hastily removed the items from the grass.

That story is LeBron regularly taking a helicopter to go from Philly to New York City, where he is reportedly settling while playing for the 76ers. It has caused an uproar across social media because some people feel he's not fully committing to his new team.

James is regularly riding a chopper to commute between Manhattan and Philadelphia for both practices and games. The flight takes about 30 to 45 minutes, which is much better than a drive in traffic that will double that time.

He is also using a corporate helicopter that is provided through his endorsement deal with Fanatics. It does not involve the 76ers at all, but it seems that it's the fans who are not big fans of this move.

articles.title: Ten-player Brighton win at Sunderland to stay third
articles.summary: High-flying Brighton and Hove Albion won 2-0 at Sunderland to make it three straight Premier League wins without conceding despite having to play more than half an hour with ten men.
body: Fabian Hurzeler's side backed up their dominant 3-0 home victory over champions Arsenal before the international break with an equally impressive display on Wearside thanks to second-half goals from Maxim De Cuyper and substitute Jaouen Hadjam.

Captain Pascal Gross once again controlled the game from midfield, creating the key opener eight minutes into the second period to become the oldest player to provide an assist in three successive top-flight games - at age of 35 years and 117 days - since Ryan Giggs in February 2012.

Despite Pascal Struijk being shown a straight red card just before the hour mark - after the Video Assistant Referee Neil Davies decided the centre back had hauled down Wilson Isidor as the Sunderland striker broke clear on goal - the visitors were rarely troubled thereafter, before sealing the win in stoppage time.

articles.title: Alphonse Le Grande edges Sea Lantern for historic Cesarewitch win
articles.summary: Alphonse Le Grande became only the second horse in history to win the Club Godolphin Cesarewitch twice when coming with a late rattle to foil a major gamble on Sea Lantern at Newmarket.
body: The Tony Martin-trained seven-year-old stayed on strongly under 5lb claimer Patrick McGettigan to cut down 4-1 favourite Sea Lantern who had hit the front with less than a furlong to run, with the winner landing the historic handicap by a short head. The well-backed Dawn Rising, runner-up 12 months ago, was third, with High Fibre fourth.
The victory repeated Alphonse Le Grande's 2024 win, seeing him emulate Aaim To Prosper who won the race in 2010 and 2012.

Martin - who was serving a three-month suspension which meant Cathy O'Leary held the licence when Alphonse Le Grande struck two years ago - said: "I couldn't believe it, I thought we had ruined our chances by running two weeks ago at the Curragh. But he's such a tough little horse he pulled it out the bag. He keeps turning up when we need him and on better ground he finds another gear.
"I didn't know we had got it, but I'm delighted he got the right result in the photo - I just need to make sure the jockey weighs in!
